title: Linkability of Student Submission Data
description: The student's submission data (work file, student ID, course, timestamp) could be linked to their identity across different systems or time periods, potentially enabling tracking of their academic activities and behavior patterns.

title: Identifiability of Student Identity
description: The student ID and course information in the submission could be used to uniquely identify the student, potentially exposing their identity to unauthorized parties who gain access to the data.

title: Disclosure of Assignment Work File
description: The assignment work file and personal information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through security vulnerabilities, insider threats, or improper access controls in the Grades Portal Web App.

title: Data Integrity of Submission Data
description: The submission data could be tampered with, altered, or corrupted during transmission or storage in the Grades Portal Web App, potentially affecting the authenticity and accuracy of the assignment record.

title: Usurpation of Student Identity
description: An attacker could impersonate the student to submit assignments on their behalf, potentially gaining unauthorized access to the system or submitting fraudulent work that could be attributed to the legitimate student.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Submission Data
description: Student submission data including student ID, course, file reference, and requesting role could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission from the Grades Portal Web App to the Assignment & Grading Service.
assumptions: Transmission is not adequately encrypted or access controls are insufficient

title: Data Manipulation of Grading Requests
description: Grading requests and file references could be altered in transit between the portal and the assignment service, potentially changing assignment details or file references before processing.
assumptions: Data integrity mechanisms are not properly implemented

title: Student Identification from Submission Metadata
description: Student ID and course information in the submission request could be used to identify specific students and their academic activities, potentially enabling profiling or tracking.
assumptions: Student IDs are not anonymized or pseudonymized before transmission

title: Unauthorized Access to Grading Service Data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service could expose student submission data, file references, and role information to unauthorized internal or external actors if access controls are inadequate.
assumptions: Access control mechanisms at P2 are not properly configured or enforced

title: Data Manipulation at Grading Service
description: The Assignment & Grading Service could alter grading requests, file references, or role information after receiving them from the portal, potentially affecting grade integrity.
assumptions: Input validation and integrity checks are not properly implemented at P2

title: Linkability of Student Academic Data
description: Data received at the Assignment & Grading Service could be linked with other student records, course enrollment data, or institutional databases, creating comprehensive profiles of students.
assumptions: Data is stored in systems that can be cross-referenced with other datasets

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Assignment Data
description: Assignment files containing student IDs, course information, and submission times could be accessed by unauthorized parties if the datastore lacks proper access controls and encryption.

title: Student Identification from Stored Data
description: The stored assignment data includes student IDs which can directly identify individuals, creating privacy risks if accessed by unauthorized parties.

title: Unauthorized Modification of Assignment Records
description: Assignment files and metadata could be altered by unauthorized actors, potentially affecting academic integrity and student records.

title: Linkability of Assignment Data to Other Records
description: Student IDs in assignment data could be used to link this information with other student records, creating comprehensive profiles of students.

title: Regulatory Compliance Violations
description: Storing student personal data may violate educational privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) if proper consent, retention policies, and data protection measures are not implemented.

title: Unauthorized Access to Teacher Account
description: Teacher account could be compromised through weak authentication, allowing unauthorized individuals to access student submission queues and potentially view or manipulate student data.
assumptions: Authentication mechanism is not sufficiently robust; attacker has access to teacher credentials or can bypass authentication.

title: Inappropriate Disclosure of Student Submission Data
description: Student submission data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through the teacher's access to the submission queue, potentially exposing sensitive student information beyond intended recipients.
assumptions: Teacher has access to all submissions without proper access controls; student data is not adequately protected during transmission or storage.

title: Linkability of Teacher Identity to Student Submissions
description: Teacher's identity could be linked to specific student submissions they review, creating a trail that connects teacher actions to student data access patterns.
assumptions: System logs teacher access to submissions; no anonymization or pseudonymization of teacher identity in logs.

title: Excessive Data Collection in Submission Queue
description: Grades Portal Web App may collect more student submission data than necessary for the teacher's review task, including metadata that could be used to infer additional information about students.
assumptions: System collects full submission content, timestamps, and metadata without applying data minimization principles.

title: Identification of Teacher Through Access Patterns
description: Teacher could be identified through their unique access patterns to specific courses and submission queues, potentially revealing their role or teaching assignments.
assumptions: Access logs contain identifiable information about which courses and submissions each teacher views.

title: Student Identifiability in Submission Display
description: Student names and work content are directly displayed to the teacher, making students identifiable through their submissions. This creates a privacy risk as student identities are exposed in the portal.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Submissions
description: Student work content, names, and submission times could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if teacher access controls are compromised or if the portal is accessed without proper authentication.

title: Linkability of Student Data Across Systems
description: Student submission data (names, work content, times) could be linked with other student records or external data sources, potentially creating a comprehensive profile of students beyond the intended scope.

title: Teacher Access Misuse of Student Data
description: The teacher (EE3) may have excessive access to student data beyond grading needs, potentially leading to misuse or unauthorized sharing of student submissions and personal information.

title: Student and Grader Identification via Feedback
description: The feedback text and associated student/grader IDs could be used to identify specific students and teachers, especially if feedback is visible to other users or stored in accessible logs.
assumptions: Feedback is stored in a retrievable format and IDs are not anonymized

title: Unauthorized Access to Grades and Feedback
description: Grades and written feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if access controls are inadequate, potentially revealing student performance and teacher evaluation practices.
assumptions: Access controls may not be properly implemented or enforced

title: Linkability of Student and Teacher Data
description: The combination of student ID, grader ID, grade, and feedback could be used to link multiple data points to create a comprehensive profile of a student or teacher.
assumptions: Multiple data flows or records exist that can be correlated

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Grading Actions
description: Teachers may be unable to prove they submitted specific grades or feedback, or students may deny receiving certain feedback, leading to disputes.
assumptions: No audit trail or digital signature mechanism is in place

title: Inadequate Data Retention and Deletion
description: Grades and feedback may be retained longer than necessary, increasing the risk of future unauthorized disclosure or misuse of historical data.
assumptions: Data retention policies are not clearly defined or enforced

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: Grade records containing student IDs, grades, and feedback could be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems, leading to privacy violations and potential academic misconduct.
assumptions: Database access controls are not properly implemented or are bypassed

title: Student Identification Through Grade Data
description: Grade records with student IDs and course information can be used to identify specific students, potentially exposing their academic performance to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Student IDs are not properly anonymized or masked

title: Linkability of Academic Records
description: Student IDs in grade records can be linked to other student data systems, creating a comprehensive profile of student activities across multiple platforms.
assumptions: Student IDs are used consistently across different systems

title: Excessive Data Collection in Feedback Field
description: The feedback field may contain unnecessary personal information or detailed comments that exceed what is needed for grading purposes, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Feedback field is not properly scoped or validated

title: Lack of Grading Action Non-Repudiation
description: Without proper audit trails, graders could deny having submitted grades or feedback, making it difficult to resolve disputes or verify grading integrity.
assumptions: No comprehensive logging or audit mechanism exists for grading actions

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Grades
description: Student grades and feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized parties (e.g., other students, employers, or third parties) through insecure data transmission or improper access controls in the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Grades are sensitive personal information that should remain confidential to the student and authorized educational personnel only.

title: Student Identity Impersonation
description: An attacker could impersonate a student to access their grades and feedback by exploiting weak authentication mechanisms or credential theft.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may not be sufficiently robust to prevent unauthorized access to student accounts.

title: Grade Data Tampering
description: Grades and feedback could be modified, deleted, or corrupted by unauthorized actors, compromising data integrity and potentially affecting academic records.
assumptions: The system may lack adequate integrity controls to prevent unauthorized modification of grade data.

title: Linkability of Grades to Student Identity
description: Student grades could be linked to their identity in ways that create privacy risks, such as enabling profiling or tracking of academic performance across contexts.
assumptions: Grades are inherently tied to student identity, and this linkage could be exploited for privacy-invasive purposes.

title: Student Identification from Grades Data
description: The Grades Portal Web App could inadvertently identify students from their grades data, especially if grades are displayed in contexts where students are not expected to be identified.
assumptions: Grades data may contain identifying information or be displayed in ways that reveal student identity.

title: Unauthorized Access to Student Grades
description: Student grades and teacher feedback could be accessed by unauthorized parties if the portal lacks proper authentication and access controls.
assumptions: Portal has insufficient security controls or authentication mechanisms are weak.

title: Student Identification from Grades
description: Student could be identified from their grades and feedback if displayed with identifying information or if grades are unique enough to identify the student.
assumptions: Grades are displayed with student identifiers or are unique enough to identify the student.

title: Linkability of Student Data
description: Student grades could be linked to other data about the student (e.g., personal information, other courses) creating a comprehensive profile.
assumptions: Grades are stored or displayed in a way that allows correlation with other student data.

title: Student Impersonation
description: An attacker could impersonate a student to access their grades and feedback if authentication is weak or compromised.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are not robust enough to prevent impersonation.

title: Excessive Data Disclosure
description: More detailed grades or feedback than necessary may be disclosed to the student, potentially revealing sensitive academic information.
assumptions: Portal displays detailed performance data that exceeds what is necessary for the student's purpose.

title: Unauthorized Account Access
description: Parent's account credentials could be compromised, allowing unauthorized parties to access child's grades
assumptions: Parent uses weak password or credentials are intercepted

title: Unauthorized Grade Disclosure
description: Child's grades could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties during transmission or storage
assumptions: Data is transmitted over insecure channel or stored without proper encryption

title: Child Identifiability from Grades
description: Grades data could be used to identify the specific child, potentially revealing sensitive information about the student
assumptions: Grades are combined with other data points that could identify the child

title: Request Linkability
description: Parent's grade requests could be linked across sessions, creating a profile of the parent's engagement with the system
assumptions: System logs request patterns that could be correlated

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child's Academic Data
description: Child's grades, feedback, and submission history could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through insecure transmission or improper access controls in the Grades Portal Web App.

title: Linkability of Academic Data with Other Records
description: The child's academic data could be linked with other personal information or school records, creating a comprehensive profile that exceeds the intended scope of the data sharing.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grades Portal
description: Unauthorized individuals could access the Grades Portal Web App and view sensitive academic information about the child, including grades and submission history.

title: Improper Identification of Authorized Parent
description: The system may fail to properly verify that the parent accessing the data is the authorized guardian, potentially allowing unauthorized family members or others to access the child's academic records.

title: Misrepresentation of Academic Performance
description: The grades, feedback, or submission history displayed to the parent could be inaccurate, outdated, or manipulated, leading to incorrect understanding of the child's academic standing.
uncertainty_note: Less certain about data manipulation risks in this context

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student/Parent Information
description: School Administrator (EE4) has access to sensitive personal data including names, emails, roles, and parent-child relationships. There is a risk that this information could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties, either intentionally or through accidental exposure during account management operations.
assumptions: Administrator has legitimate access but may share data inappropriately or system lacks proper access controls

title: Malicious Modification of Account Data
description: School Administrator (EE4) can create, modify, and disable accounts and parent-child links. There is a risk of malicious alteration of sensitive information such as names, emails, roles, or relationships, potentially leading to identity fraud, unauthorized access, or data integrity issues.
assumptions: Administrator account may be compromised or administrator may act maliciously

title: Administrator Identity Impersonation
description: There is a risk that an unauthorized individual could impersonate the School Administrator (EE4) to gain access to the Grades Portal Web App (P1) and perform unauthorized account management operations, potentially compromising student and parent data.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be weak or administrator credentials may be compromised

title: Inadvertent Data Exposure During Account Operations
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) processes sensitive account and relationship data. There is a risk that during account creation, modification, or disabling operations, data could be inadvertently exposed through logging, error messages, or improper data handling.
assumptions: System may lack proper data sanitization or logging controls

title: Unauthorized Modification of Account Records
description: The Assignment & Grading Service writes account records to the Account Directory. Unauthorized actors could potentially modify these records, leading to incorrect account information, altered parent-child relationships, or fraudulent grading data.
assumptions: The system lacks adequate access controls or audit logging for write operations to the Account Directory.

title: Tampering with Parent-Child Relationship Links
description: The grading service writes parent-child relationship links to the Account Directory. Malicious actors could tamper with these links to create false relationships between individuals, potentially for identity fraud or social engineering purposes.
assumptions: Parent-child relationship data is sensitive and could be exploited if modified without authorization.

title: Linkability of Account Records via Parent-Child Links
description: Parent-child relationship links written to the Account Directory could be used to link different account records together, potentially revealing family relationships between individuals without their consent.
assumptions: The Account Directory stores identifiable information that can be correlated across records.

title: Identification of Individuals via Account Records
description: Account records written to the Account Directory contain personally identifiable information that could be used to identify individuals, potentially exposing sensitive personal data.
assumptions: Account records include identifiers such as names, IDs, or other PII.

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Grading Operations
description: When the Assignment & Grading Service writes account records, there may be insufficient audit trails to prevent denial of actions, making it difficult to verify who made specific changes to the Account Directory.
assumptions: The system does not implement comprehensive logging and authentication for write operations.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Educational Data
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transmitted to third-party cloud hosting provider, creating risk of unauthorized disclosure if provider lacks adequate access controls and encryption.

title: Data Integrity Compromise During Transmission
description: Nightly backup data in transit to cloud provider could be intercepted or altered by malicious actors, potentially corrupting grade records and assignment data.

title: Linkability of Student Records
description: Account directory and grade records contain personally identifiable information that could be linked to specific students, enabling profiling or tracking of academic performance.

title: Identification of Individuals from Backup Data
description: Full account directory and grade records enable identification of students and staff, creating privacy risks if data is accessed by unauthorized parties.

title: User Unawareness of Third-Party Data Sharing
description: Students and staff may not be informed that their grade records and account information are being replicated to external cloud hosting provider.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance Risk
description: Transfer of educational data to third-party cloud provider may violate data protection regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) if proper consent, data minimization, and cross-border transfer safeguards are not implemented.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: Grade records database may be accessed by unauthorized individuals or systems, exposing sensitive academic performance data of students.
assumptions: Access controls are not properly implemented or are bypassed

title: Student Identification from Grade Records
description: Grade records contain personally identifiable information that could be used to identify specific students, potentially leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: Grade records are not properly anonymized or pseudonymized

title: Linkability of Grade Data with Other Records
description: Grade records could be linked with other student data (demographics, attendance, behavioral records) to create comprehensive profiles of students.
assumptions: Multiple data sources are accessible and can be correlated

title: Excessive Data Sharing Across Views
description: Assignment & Grading Service may share more grade data with parent and teacher views than necessary, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Data sharing policies are not strictly enforced across different user views

title: Inappropriate Data Exposure to Parents
description: Grade records may be exposed to parents beyond what is educationally necessary, potentially revealing sensitive academic information.
assumptions: Parent access controls are not properly configured
